result.evidence: Internal design gap; no external premise is needed. The whole root/nested/task bundle was read. The missing boundary is user invocation to inspected attempt: artifact.md:53 gives recover REF with only a decision/pane selector, while :79 requires an exact attempt and :85 promises ready guarded recovery argv preserving attempt information. Neither those sections, the inherited nested specs, nor ht-qhz.6 defines REF as attempt-qualified or supplies an expected-attempt/invocation identity. Concrete sequence: (1) reserve attempt A and lose its reply/result; :69 and :71 leave A possible_creation/outcome_unknown and require recovery guidance. The operator inspects A and retains the displayed --not-created invocation. (2) A valid recovery records no effect and permits a distinct next attempt (:81); its response can be lost, or another operator can make that decision. (3) ordinary agent retry reserves B under the same immutable bootstrap, then B also becomes uncertain (:69, :71, :81). Both invocations have ended, so the known-in-flight lock refusal in :81 does not stop the scenario. (4) repeating the retained command has no specified input distinguishing replay of the assertion about A from a fresh assertion about B. If dispatch selects current B and derives B's deterministic recovery child key (:63), its canonical decision is individually unique and noncontradictory, yet closes B using inspection of A. This breaks the intended exact-attempt assertion binding (:79, :81) and the presentation-only recovery replay requirement (:81); an ensuing retry can create again without any inspected noncreation assertion for B. Always selecting A instead prevents this replay error but leaves the documented command unable to address B unless REF semantics are extended. The accepted limit (:83) permits an operator's mistaken noncreation/quiescence assertion; it does not accept silently moving a correct A assertion onto B. An attempt-qualified REF could solve this within the displayed grammar, but defining and requiring that binding in emitted argv is precisely the omitted contract, rather than an existing mitigation.
